request.spec:
The sheet's settings assign a role to a user name: clerk (the default for any name) or steward
(ROLE_SET user=<name> role=<role>). The sheet also has a clerk limit (two decimals; blank means no
limit; SETTING_CHANGED key=clerk-limit value=<limit>). A clerk can settle a claim only when its
due is at or below the limit; above it, settling is refused with an error on the claim. A claim
whose due is n/a is within any limit. Stewards settle anything. The opener still cannot settle
their own claim.

agent.result_text:
Roles and the clerk limit are in, and all 4 Playwright tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` pass under `bin/e2e`.

**How settling works now:** when someone settles a claim, the server looks up their role on the sheet. A name with no role set is a clerk.
- A clerk is refused if the sheet has a clerk limit and the claim's due is above it. The claim shows its `claim-error` and nothing is written to the store or the audit file.
- A due of n/a is treated as within any limit.
- A steward can settle anything.
- The person who opened a claim still can't settle it, whatever their role.

The check happens before anything is written, using the same due figure that settling would fix (`ApplyClaimStatus.java`).

**Settings:** a new Settings panel has the clerk-limit field and shows the value in force. The limit must be 0.00 or more with up to two decimals; blank means no limit. Every save writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=clerk-limit value=<limit>`, even when the value doesn't change, because the test expects that. A bad value shows `settings-error`. The endpoints are `GET` and `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/settings`.

**Roles:** a new Roles panel lets you give a user name the role clerk or steward, and lists the roles given. Anything else, or a blank name, is refused with `role-form-error`. Each save writes `ROLE_SET … user=<name> role=<role>`. The endpoints are `GET` and `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/roles`.

**Behaviour the request didn't spell out:**
- Anyone signed in can change roles and the clerk limit; the test has a steward and a clerk both saving the limit.
- When there is no limit, the "current" value shows as empty text.
- A refused blank limit writes `value=` with nothing after it.

The data is in two new migrations, `V17__setting.sql` and `V18__user_role.sql`. The claim error message now also mentions the clerk limit.
